newsitem.title: UK: Most OPEC ministers, Lukman expected at Goa talks.
newsitem.headline: Most OPEC ministers, Lukman expected at Goa talks.

text.p: Most of OPEC's 11 oil ministers and Secretary General Rilwanu Lukman are expected to attend talks between oil producers and consumers in Goa, India on December 6-8, OPEC sources said. The sources said influential Saudi Oil Minister Ali Ibrahim Naimi is among ministers from the Organisation of the Petroleum Exprting Countries (OPEC) expected to participate in the roundtable informal discussions on issues related to oil supply and demand.
It will be the fifth such meeting of the world's largest oil producers and consumers and will take place just days after a late November meeting of OPEC ministers in Vienna.
The first producer-consumer gathering was held in 1991 in Paris and the last time the two sides got together was in September 1995 in Puerto La Cruz, Venezuela.
At the Puerto La Cruz meeting, Naimi warned oil companies against running oil inventories too low to cut operating costs.
His words are coming back to haunt them as oil prices hover around post-Gulf War highs as oil companies rush to replenish low heating fuel stocks before peak winter demand hits, analysts say.
"These meeting with consumers are always worthwhile. We usually have interesting things to say to each other," an OPEC source said.
